questions.question_text: A clinician is considering combination therapy for treatment-resistant depression. Which of the following combinations has the most potential for serious adverse reactions?
questions.explanation: Serious adverse reactions, sometimes fatal, with features resembling serotonin syndrome and neuroleptic malignant syndrome have been reported when venlafaxine and tranylcypromine are used together.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is most commonly comorbid with prepubertal bipolar disorder?
questions.explanation: For example, Geller et al. (1995) reported that about 90% of prepubertal (and 30% of adolescent) bipolar patients also had ADHD.

questions.question_text: A 39-year-old actuary for an insurance company is offered a substantial promotion that will require her to move to another city. Her new office will be on the 23rd floor of a high-rise building. She informs her psychiatrist that she is "terrified" of riding in an elevator and terrified of heights, but desperately wants the new job. Which of the interventions listed below is most likely to be successful for her?
questions.explanation: This woman is suffering from a specific phobia. The method that has been most studied and found most effective is behavior therapy. The behavior therapy techniques that have been employed with phobias include systematic desensitization.

questions.question_text: During resettlement, a refugee takes on the values and attitudes of the new culture and does not retain his original cultural values. Which of the following best describes this process?
questions.explanation: Assimilation entails making contacts with the new culture while shedding one's own cultural values.

questions.question_text: Parasomnias can be differentiated from dyssomnias because parasomnias involve abnormalities in which of the following aspects of sleep?

options.text: Physiological systems that occur during sleep

correct_answer.text: Physiological systems that occur during sleep

correct_answers.text: Physiological systems that occur during sleep

questions.explanation: The factors listed in the other options are affected in dyssomnias.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old male patient with an initial episode of schizophrenia is treated with risperidone. After 1 week of treatment he no longer experiences agitation. By the third week of treatment, with gradual titration of risperidone to 6 mg daily, his delusions and hallucinations are significantly improved. At week 4, he describes some trouble sleeping at night because of restlessness but reports that he is much less fearful and no longer hears voices. When seen for a scheduled appointment at week 6, however, he is noticeably drooling and is in constant motion, rocking back and forth and fidgeting in his chair. The side effect of treatment that he is most likely experiencing is:
questions.explanation: Akathisia consists of a subjective feeling of restlessness along with restless movements, usually in the legs or feet, which may be mistaken for ongoing psychosis with associated agitation.

questions.question_text: A patient takes a medication for bipolar disorder throughout pregnancy and delivery. The newborn is noted to be cyanotic and in respiratory distress. An echocardiogram reveals significant displacement of two leaflets of the tricuspid valve into the ventricle and a large atrial septal defect consistent with Ebstein's anomaly. Which of the following is the woman most likely taking during her pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Lithium is the only psychoactive, non-anticonvulsant drug that is thought to be associated with the specific heart defect.

questions.question_text: A forensic psychiatric evaluation differs from a general psychiatric evaluation in that a forensic evaluation:

options.text: does not have a doctor-patient relationship.
requires the presence of a lawyer during the evaluation.
typically includes a mental status examination.

correct_answer.text: does not have a doctor-patient relationship.

correct_answers.text: does not have a doctor-patient relationship.

questions.explanation: A forensic evaluation essentially includes a general psychiatric evaluation within its context.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man reports that he is unable to sleep and hears noises and voices at night even though he lives alone. The symptoms started abruptly on the day preceding the visit. During the interview, he repeatedly brushes off his arms, muttering about bugs. The information that would be most helpful in determining initial interventions would be the history of:
questions.explanation: Psychotic symptoms may be due to a general medical condition, may be medication induced, or may be induced by substances of abuse.

questions.question_text: The obtaining of informed consent from an individual prior to initiating any treatment fulfills which of the following ethical principles?
questions.explanation: Autonomy is the ethical principle that is relevant to obtaining informed consent.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotherapies has the best documented effectiveness in the treatment of major depressive disorder?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal and cognitive behavior therapy are the best documented psychotherapeutic treatments for major depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants would be the best choice for a patient concerned about erectile dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Most antidepressants other than bupropion have significant rates of erectile dysfunction as well as other aspects of sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: The National Comorbidity Survey identified a number of gender differences in exposure and in the development of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Compared with females, males have:

options.text: the same trauma exposure, and the same prevalence of PTSD.
higher trauma exposure, and higher prevalence of PTSD.
lower trauma exposure, and lower prevalence of PTSD.
higher trauma exposure, and lower prevalence of PTSD.
lower trauma exposure, and higher prevalence of PTSD.

correct_answer.text: higher trauma exposure, and lower prevalence of PTSD.

correct_answers.text: higher trauma exposure, and lower prevalence of PTSD.

questions.explanation: Males are more likely than females to be exposed to traumatic events; females are more likely than males to develop PTSD.

questions.question_text: A cancer patient with significant nausea requires an antidepressant. Which of the following medications would be the best choice?
questions.explanation: With the exception of mirtazapine, all of the drugs listed have been shown in clinical trials to cause considerably more nausea than placebo.

questions.question_text: When non-substance abusing men and women drink the same amount of alcohol, the women are likely to have higher alcohol blood levels than the men. The best explanation for this is that compared with men, women:

options.text: metabolize less alcohol in the gut.
have a larger volume of distribution.

correct_answer.text: metabolize less alcohol in the gut.

correct_answers.text: metabolize less alcohol in the gut.

questions.explanation: Women metabolize less alcohol in the gut, resulting in higher blood alcohol concentrations after consuming the same amount of alcohol as men.

questions.question_text: Which of the following situations best describes when weight considerations should determine hospitalization for anorexia nervosa in children and young adolescents?

options.text: Weight is fluctuating unpredictably over 2-3 months.
Weight is being rapidly lost and outpatient efforts are ineffective, regardless of actual weight.
Weight is less than 20% of recommended healthy body weight.
Weight is less than 25% of ideal body weight.

correct_answer.text: Weight is being rapidly lost and outpatient efforts are ineffective, regardless of actual weight.

correct_answers.text: Weight is being rapidly lost and outpatient efforts are ineffective, regardless of actual weight.

questions.explanation: In younger children and adolescents hospitalization should be considered when the patient is losing weight rapidly and before too much weight loss occurs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotic drugs is most likely to be associated with hyperprolactinemia?
questions.explanation: Risperidone causes prolactin elevations that are similar to those caused by high-potency dopamine antagonist antipsychotic medications.

questions.question_text: Which of the following atypical antipsychotic drugs is a D2 receptor partial agonist?
questions.explanation: A partial agonist is an agonist that cannot maximally activate a receptor regardless of the concentration of drug present.

questions.question_text: A 33-year-old man started twice-weekly psychodynamic psychotherapy 6 months ago with the goal of exploring issues stemming from his distant relationship with his father and his inability to form adequate mentoring relationships in his work as a research chemist. He reports an increasing preoccupation with his therapist's unwillingness to see him more frequently. The patient has been speaking in therapy of his wish that the therapist see him on Sunday. He believes that the therapist refuses to have extra sessions because he prefers other patients. Which of the following best explains the patient's behavior?
questions.explanation: This is an example of classic transference that reenacts aspects of his childhood relationship with his father.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders has the highest relative risk for first-degree relatives?
questions.explanation: The relative risk for bipolar disorder is around 25.

questions.question_text: A 68-year-old man has a grand mal seizure that is attributed to an abrupt hyponatremia, with a serum sodium concentration of 110 mmol/L. Which of the following medications is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: According to the oxcarbazepine package insert, clinically significant hyponatremia (serum sodium <125 mmol/L) developed in 2.5% of patients in controlled studies of epilepsy.

questions.question_text: Social rhythm therapy, which is designed specifically for bipolar disorder, is based on which of the following models?

options.text: Object relations and self psychology theory
Cognitive therapy techniques to address social dysfunction

questions.explanation: Social rhythm therapy grew from a chronobiological model of bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: Rapid cycling in bipolar I or II disorder is associated with:
questions.explanation: Rapid cycling in bipolar disorder is defined as more mood episodes in the previous 12 months.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old woman has a history of a left frontal lobe stroke. Which of the following psychiatric symptoms is most commonly associated with a stroke in this area of the brain?
questions.explanation: Poststroke depression has been documented after cerebrovascular accidents occurring in many areas in the brain.

questions.question_text: Genetic studies of obsessive-compulsive disorder have revealed linkages to which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Genetic studies of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder have revealed high family rates of Tourette's syndrome.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist proposes to use an FDA-approved drug not previously used for the treatment of mania because it has biochemical properties similar to known antimanic agents. The psychiatrist has also read several articles describing open-label studies suggesting efficacy of the drug. The patient in question has not responded to any agent thus far. The psychiatrist must do which of the following?

options.text: Notify the FDA, since the drug is being used for a non-FDA-approved purpose.
Wait until there is higher-quality data to support this use of the drug.
Obtain informed consent from the patient or from an appropriate proxy agent.
Get an institutional review board approval, since what is proposed is clinical research.

correct_answer.text: Obtain informed consent from the patient or from an appropriate proxy agent.

correct_answers.text: Obtain informed consent from the patient or from an appropriate proxy agent.

questions.explanation: When all available treatments have failed, a nonstandard approach based on limited evidence may be all that is available, provided that proper precautions are taken.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old retired physicist who is suffering from metastatic cancer is referred to a psychiatrist by the primary care physician because the patient wants to die and has requested assistance in suicide. On evaluation, the psychiatrist finds that the patient's cognition is intact. The most appropriate next step for the psychiatrist is to:

options.text: find out whether there are areas of suffering that can be addressed by available palliative care measures.
tell the referring physician that the patient can be given assistance in suicide because the patient is a competent adult.
be as persuasive as possible so that the patient accepts the cancer treatment.
tell the referring physician that even though the patient's cognition appears intact, the patient is probably incapacitated by virtue of the unreasonable choice that is being made.

correct_answer.text: find out whether there are areas of suffering that can be addressed by available palliative care measures.

correct_answers.text: find out whether there are areas of suffering that can be addressed by available palliative care measures.

questions.explanation: Most patients who request assisted suicide eventually change their minds when the sources of their suffering are better addressed.

questions.question_text: Of the following ethnic groups, which is at lowest risk of completed suicide?
questions.explanation: Most studies have demonstrated that Caucasians are at highest risk of suicide, followed in order by Native Americans, African Americans, Hispanic Americans, and Asian Americans.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old boy is referred for psychiatric evaluation after taking an overdose of an over-the-counter cold medication. The patient denies that this was a suicide attempt. The patient acknowledges that he has been having difficulties for about a year, since the separation of his parents. He often feels angry and irritable, has difficulty sleeping, has little appetite, has lost weight, has little interest in his usual activities, and often wishes he was dead. His grades have dropped to the point that he is failing his courses. Over the past year, he has been smoking 1-2 packs of cigarettes a day, drinking to the point of intoxication on the weekends, and taking over-the-counter cold medication to enhance the effects of the alcohol. His past psychiatric history is significant for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), for which he has a prescription for a stimulant medication. He has not taken his medication as prescribed. Instead, he hoards the medication and then takes large quantities to experience a euphoric effect. Which of the following medications would be the most efficacious in addressing this patient's symptom constellation?
questions.explanation: Bupropion is effective in the treatment of many types of depression and has been shown to be effective in assisting with both smoking cessation and improving the core symptoms of ADHD.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist attends a dinner lecture sponsored by a major pharmaceutical company, the maker of a newly approved drug for major depression. The company's representative approaches the psychiatrist after the lecture and says, "I hope we can count on you to prescribe our medication. This is a great medication!" The psychiatrist does not know what to say and later feels troubled by this encounter. Which of the following statements reflects the psychiatrist's ethical obligation in this situation?

options.text: The psychiatrist should be aware that "strings attached" industry-sponsored activities are unethical.
The psychiatrist can accept dinners and "repay" the company with favorable prescribing practices if the psychiatrist chooses to do so.
The psychiatrist must repay the representative for the cost of the dinner, since there are apparent, though unstated, ethical conflicts.
The psychiatrist should report the pharmaceutical representative's behavior to the local APA branch's ethics committee.

correct_answer.text: The psychiatrist should be aware that "strings attached" industry-sponsored activities are unethical.

correct_answers.text: The psychiatrist should be aware that "strings attached" industry-sponsored activities are unethical.

questions.explanation: Gifts should not be accepted if strings are attached.

questions.question_text: More severe and prolonged forms of conduct disorder are most often associated with which of the following comorbid disorders?
questions.explanation: More severe and prolonged conduct disorder is associated with early onset, comorbid ADHD, and conduct symptoms that are more frequent, numerous, and varied.

questions.question_text: A 62-year-old man is taking desipramine for depression. He presents with marked sedation, tachycardia, and postural hypotension about 10 days after the addition of a second antidepressant. Which of the following medications is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Desipramine is a substrate for cytochrome P450 2D6. Of the drugs listed, only fluoxetine is a potent inhibitor of this enzyme.

questions.question_text: Which of the following diseases associated with dementia characteristically has early changes in personality and a late decline in memory?
questions.explanation: Pick's disease specifically affects the frontal and temporal lobes, accounting for the early signs of personality changes, loss of social skills, and emotional blunting.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features best distinguishes anorexia nervosa from bulimia nervosa?

options.text: Calluses on the dorsum of the hand

questions.explanation: Decreased body weight is a defining feature of anorexia nervosa, whereas persons with bulimia nervosa typically have normal body weight.

questions.question_text: Which CNS structure is most responsible for arousal and sleep-wake cycles?
questions.explanation: The reticular activating system modulates arousal, wake cycles, and conscious activity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following aspects of cognitive performance is most likely to decline in the course of normal aging?
questions.explanation: Speed of learning, processing speed, and speed of performance of cognitive tasks tend to decline with normal aging.

questions.question_text: Disorders with significant psychiatric symptoms that can be linked to a single gene include:
questions.explanation: Only fragile X syndrome is due to a single gene.

questions.question_text: The rule of confidentiality is waived in a psychiatrist-patient interaction when the treatment or evaluation includes:

options.text: a patient who reveals a past felony.

questions.explanation: When a psychiatrist is examining a patient for forensic purposes, the individual must be informed that information collected will be shared with the party that engaged the psychiatrist.

questions.question_text: The highest percentage of persons with mental retardation have an intelligence quotient of:
questions.explanation: Up to 85% of persons with mental retardation have an IQ between 50 and 70.

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old girl who has been cared for in seven different foster homes since the age of 6 months now exhibits excessive familiarity with strangers. Her current foster parents, with whom she has lived for the past 5 months, state that she does not seem to be particularly close to them. The girl's biological mother is reported to have used alcohol in a binge pattern during her pregnancy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The girl's indiscriminate sociability is behavior typical of reactive attachment disorder, disinhibited type.

questions.question_text: An 8-year-old girl insists on keeping a rigid routine when dressing, will wear only certain clothes, insists on recopying her homework if there are any mistakes, and has temper tantrums when the items on her desk are moved. During a discussion of the diagnosis and treatment options, her parents express reluctance to use medication and want to explore other options. The first recommendation would be:
questions.explanation: Cognitive behavior therapy has been demonstrated to be effective in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are common hyperarousal symptoms in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)?

options.text: Intense psychological distress at exposure to external cues resembling the trauma

questions.explanation: Symptoms of hyperarousal include persistent symptoms of anxiety or increased arousal, difficulty falling or staying asleep, irritability, and hypervigilance.

questions.question_text: Which medication is considered first-line monotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder?
questions.explanation: Sertraline is FDA approved for the treatment of PTSD.

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old woman has a long history of difficulty with driving because she worries that she might hit a car or a person accidentally. She also worries excessively about her son getting hurt or attacked when he goes out. Her husband can often reassure her. Which of the following diagnoses is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The worries that occur in generalized anxiety disorder are about everyday events and are responsive to reassurance.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman with chronic headaches has undergone trials with several narcotic and nonnarcotic agents with variable success. Her physician elects to try her on a newer antidepressant medication. Which of the following medications is most likely to be effective?
questions.explanation: Venlafaxine is seen to be more promising as an analgesic compared to nefazodone, mirtazapine, or bupropion.

questions.question_text: Echolalia and echopraxia are most likely manifestations of which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Echolalia and echopraxia can characterize catatonic depression.

questions.question_text: An adolescent female took an unknown drug at an all-night dance party. She was brought to the emergency department for evaluation of altered mental status and marked hyperthermia. Which of the following was most likely the drug that was ingested?
questions.explanation: MDMA has been reported to cause severe adverse effects, including altered mental status and hyperthermia.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old man who is hospitalized for psychosis displays prominent, excessive, and purposeless motor activity together with peculiar voluntary movements. On one occasion, he stands in the middle of the ward immobile and mute. He demonstrates waxy flexibility. The appropriate medical intervention is:
questions.explanation: Lorazepam improves catatonia dramatically.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old woman is referred for treatment of chronic, severe major depression. Which of the following treatment approaches is most likely to be associated with sustained improvement in her symptoms?
questions.explanation: Recent studies now support combined psychotherapy and antidepressant therapy for chronic depression.

questions.question_text: In people with typical left brain dominance, the ability to interpret the emotional tone of speech is a function of the:
questions.explanation: The corresponding area in the nondominant hemisphere interprets the emotional tone of speech.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotherapies has the greatest body of evidence demonstrating efficacy for social phobia?
questions.explanation: Cognitive behavioral psychotherapy incorporates cognitive input which is crucial for treatment success in social phobia.

questions.question_text: A patient who is completely deaf arrives with an interpreter at the outpatient clinic for an evaluation of depressed mood. You wish to know about the patient's sleep quality. Of the following, which is the most appropriate way to work with the interpreter and the patient?

options.text: Look at the patient and ask, "How are you sleeping?"
Ask the interpreter, "How is she sleeping?"
Write out "How are you sleeping?" and give it to the patient.
Loudly enunciate "How are you sleeping?" to the patient.
Ask the interpreter, "Please ask her how she is sleeping."

correct_answer.text: Look at the patient and ask, "How are you sleeping?"

correct_answers.text: Look at the patient and ask, "How are you sleeping?"

questions.explanation: One should always address the patient directly while the interpreter translates.

questions.question_text: An internist consults a psychiatrist because of his frustration with an elderly patient who has a diagnosis of hypochondriasis. Medical tests are negative, but the patient is unable to accept that he is not ill. The psychiatrist confirms the diagnosis of hypochondriasis. Which of the following is the best management strategy for a patient with hypochondriasis?

options.text: See the patient as needed, but for a limited time.
Refer the patient to a more psychologically minded internist colleague.
Have regularly scheduled appointments with limited reassurance.
Instruct the patient to call only for urgent matters.

correct_answer.text: Have regularly scheduled appointments with limited reassurance.

correct_answers.text: Have regularly scheduled appointments with limited reassurance.

questions.explanation: Regularly scheduled appointments with limited reassurance appears to be more effective in managing hypochondriasis.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old woman presents for an initial evaluation. She describes periods of mood lability and unstable interpersonal relationships, particularly with men. During periods of stress, she reports feeling angry and "empty" and sometimes scratches herself with sharp items. Sleep is often a problem, and alprazolam has been helpful. In developing a treatment plan, which of the following principles would be most appropriate?

options.text: Target specific symptoms that are currently causing disruption.
pharmacotherapy to antidepressants and mood stabilizers.
Treat with multiple classes of medications for potential future symptoms.
Withhold medications if the patient engages in acting out behavior.

correct_answer.text: Target specific symptoms that are currently causing disruption.

correct_answers.text: Target specific symptoms that are currently causing disruption.

questions.explanation: Patients require a flexible, targeted approach.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman with bipolar disorder who has been successfully maintained on lithium presents at the clinic with the complaint of swelling in her ankles. Examination reveals 2+ pitting edema. Her serum lithium level is 0.8 mEq/L. The physician prescribes a thiazide diuretic. Four days later the patient presents at the emergency department with confusion, a coarse tremor in her extremities, and ataxia. Her serum lithium level is now 2.6 mEq/L. Urinalysis reveals a slightly elevated specific gravity and an absence of blood, ketones, and protein. Which of the following best explains the patient's lithium toxicity?

options.text: Increased reabsorption in the proximal tubules

correct_answer.text: Increased reabsorption in the proximal tubules

correct_answers.text: Increased reabsorption in the proximal tubules

questions.explanation: When the body has a sodium deficiency, such as occurs with the administration of sodium-depleting diuretics, the kidneys compensate by reabsorbing more sodium, and along with it, lithium.

questions.question_text: A random community sample contains 100 individuals who meet diagnostic criteria for borderline personality disorder. Which of the following is the best estimate of the gender ratio of the sample?
questions.explanation: Borderline personality disorder is diagnosed predominantly in women, with an estimated female-to-male ratio of 3:1.

questions.question_text: The Child Behavior Checklist is a commonly used instrument completed by parents about their children's behaviors. In a study comparing the results from subject groups obtained from multiple cultures, girls scored higher than boys across all cultures on which behavior scale?
questions.explanation: Across all studied cultures, girls scored higher on the anxious/depressed behavior scale.

questions.question_text: Characteristic cognitive processes in persons with obsessive-compulsive disorder include:

options.text: normal confidence in one's own memory.

questions.explanation: In persons with obsessive-compulsive disorder, a decreased capacity for selective attention is hypothesized to reflect difficulties in dismissing obsessions.

questions.question_text: In family studies of patients with schizophrenia, the personality disorder that has been found to occur most frequently in first-degree relatives is:
questions.explanation: Although all cluster A personality disorders are more common in the biological relatives of patients with schizophrenia, schizotypal is most frequently identified.

questions.question_text: The following vignette applies to questions 59 and 60. A 25-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with the chief complaint, "I think I'm having a heart attack." She reports that while grocery shopping she suddenly felt "scared to death." Her heart was racing, she felt short of breath and dizzy, and she was nauseated and broke out in a sweat. Her fingers and hands and the area around her mouth felt numb. The episode lasted about 10 minutes and dissipated on its own. Physical examination and laboratory studies, including a chest X-ray, blood chemistries, cardiac enzymes, and electrocardiogram, are normal. In the lab, which of the following substances would be most likely to induce an episode with these symptoms?
questions.explanation: Sodium lactate is one of the panic-inducing substances that can shift the acid-base balance.

questions.question_text: The medication that is most likely to be effective in the long-term treatment of her condition with the best tolerance of side effects is:
questions.explanation: Experience is showing the SSRIs, particularly paroxetine, over the benzodiazepines, monoamine oxidase inhibitors and tricyclic and tetracyclic drugs in terms of effectiveness and tolerance of adverse effects.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old man with migraine headaches had successfully obtained relief by taking codeine. Recently his physician started him on a trial of paroxetine for suspected depression. The patient notes improvement in his symptoms of depression and now has headaches less frequently, but when he does have one, he must take twice the amount of codeine for pain relief. Which of the following best describes this drug interaction?
questions.explanation: Codeine's analgesic effect is a result of its metabolism by cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP2D6. If that enzyme is inhibited—such as occurs with paroxetine—then the dose of codeine must be increased.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is most likely to be associated with substantial weight gain?
questions.explanation: Appetite increase and weight gain have been more consistently associated with mirtazapine than with the other listed antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Expert consensus suggests that the length of time for a pharmacological trial in obsessive-compulsive disorder should be at least:
questions.explanation: Trials of medications used for obsessive-compulsive disorder indicate that a daily dose for 10-12 weeks is optimal.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man presents with a 4-week history of low mood, crying spells, poor sleep with early morning awakening, poor appetite with a 12-pound weight loss, and difficulty in concentrating at work. At age 27 he had been hospitalized with an episode of mania, but shortly thereafter he decided not to continue in outpatient follow-up treatment. He has no medical problems and takes no medications. As initial pharmacotherapeutic treatment, which of the following is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Antidepressant monotherapy is not recommended given the risk of precipitating a switch into mania in patients with bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: A patient with borderline personality disorder is in dialectical behavior therapy. She has left messages on the therapist's voice-mail while he is on vacation despite an agreement that she would not call him at all during his vacation and would go to the emergency department if she became suicidal. The best approach in dialectical behavior therapy is for the therapist to:

options.text: explain to the patient that the treatment plan will have to change if she cannot keep the agreement.
make an exception since there is a history of serious attempts and safety is an issue.
wait for the patient to bring up the issue before discussing the implications for therapy.
explain that a treatment boundary has been violated and therapy will have to end.

correct_answer.text: explain to the patient that the treatment plan will have to change if she cannot keep the agreement.

correct_answers.text: explain to the patient that the treatment plan will have to change if she cannot keep the agreement.

questions.explanation: Therapists should be alert to the occurrence of boundary violations and proactive in dealing with them.

questions.question_text: A patient being treated with interferon for hepatitis C complains of depression, anxiety, and irritability. Which of the following pharmacological agents has the most evidence for efficacy in treating those symptoms?
questions.explanation: The treatment of choice for interferon's psychiatric side effects of depression, anxiety, and irritability is currently a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor such as sertraline.

questions.question_text: An 11-year-old girl is referred for an evaluation of school problems. Her teachers and parents describe her as argumentative, hostile, disrespectful, and difficult. The girl often refuses to listen, will not obey instructions, does not do her work, has temper tantrums, and insists on having her own way. She has been this way since preschool. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: The features of oppositional defiant disorder include a recurrent pattern of negativistic, defiant, disobedient, and hostile behavior toward authority figures.

questions.question_text: Patients with end-stage renal disease who are on hemodialysis are most likely to present with which of the following psychiatric symptoms?
questions.explanation: While various psychiatric symptoms can occur in hemodialysis patients, depression is the most prevalent.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old woman has had five hospitalizations over the 3-year period since she was initially diagnosed with schizophrenia. On each occasion, recurrent psychotic symptoms have been associated with treatment nonadherence. Which of the following strategies is supported by the greatest body of research evidence as the most likely to improve medication adherence for this patient?
questions.explanation: A review of studies of psychosocial interventions for improving medication adherence showed that programs that focus on the attitudinal and behavioral aspects of taking medications generally have better outcomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most likely symptom in cocaine intoxication?
questions.explanation: Cocaine intoxication can produce hypertension, tachycardia, seizures, paranoid delusions, and delirium.

questions.question_text: A consultation-liaison psychiatrist, on arriving on the internal medicine hospital unit, learns that the patient's nurse requested the consultation and that the attending internist does not want the consultation. Of the following, the best action for the psychiatrist would be to:

options.text: talk with the nurse's supervisor about the correct way to request a consultation.
proceed with the consultation and make treatment recommendations.
talk briefly with the nurse about why he or she considered the consultation important.
apologize to the attending internist and leave the unit.

correct_answer.text: talk briefly with the nurse about why he or she considered the consultation important.

correct_answers.text: talk briefly with the nurse about why he or she considered the consultation important.

questions.explanation: The liaison process includes case-finding and fostering the development of greater psychiatric knowledge.

questions.question_text: Which of the following accurately describes the major quality that fundamentally distinguishes brief dynamic psychotherapy from long-term dynamic psychotherapy? Brief therapy has:
questions.explanation: Brief therapy is structured to address a specific, limited focus with the least-radical intervention.

questions.question_text: A 68-year-old man with bipolar I disorder has been adequately maintained on lithium. His most recent serum lithium level was 0.8 mEq/L. He has a variety of medical problems for which he takes several medications. He now presents with pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased energy, and little sleep. His serum lithium level is 0.3 mEq/L. His wife reports that the patient has been adherent to his medication regimen, but she began to notice a change 2 weeks after his primary care physician started him on a new medication. What was the most likely class of medication added to his regimen?
questions.explanation: Drugs that may decrease lithium levels include xanthine bronchodilators such as theophylline and aminophylline.

questions.question_text: A patient with an alcohol problem is ambivalent about starting acamprosate. The psychiatrist explores the patient’s thoughts about the advantages and disadvantages of taking and not taking the medication, attempting to tip the patient's decisional balance in favor of taking the medication. Which of the following techniques is the physician using?
questions.explanation: Motivational enhancement therapy is a form of psychotherapy that has been shown to be effective in the treatment of substance use disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following differentiates Lewy body dementia from dementia of the Alzheimer's type?
questions.explanation: Of the core criteria for the diagnosis of dementia with Lewy bodies, visual hallucinations are particularly important in differentiation.

questions.question_text: The symptom of "flashbacks" is a manifestation of which of the following psychological states?
questions.explanation: Flashbacks are experienced by individuals suffering from PTSD.

questions.question_text: Response prevention is a useful psychotherapeutic technique for which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Response prevention techniques that decrease the frequency of rituals have been shown in clinical trials to be useful in obsessive-compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: A patient with alcohol dependence wants a psychiatrist to bill the patient's insurance company under another diagnosis because the patient is afraid of the stigma attached to the diagnosis. The psychiatrist should:

options.text: Explore the reasons behind the request and explain why this is something the psychiatrist is reluctant to do.
Tell the patient that this would be lying and refuse to comply.
Comply with the request because stigmas are inherently unfair to patients.
Comply with the request provided the patient's fears are adequately addressed.

correct_answer.text: Explore the reasons behind the request and explain why this is something the psychiatrist is reluctant to do.

correct_answers.text: Explore the reasons behind the request and explain why this is something the psychiatrist is reluctant to do.

questions.explanation: The issue of therapeutic benefit to the patient must guide the manner in which the psychiatrist works within the limits of ethics and the law.

questions.question_text: In a patient experiencing bereavement, which of the following suggests the diagnosis of major depression?
questions.explanation: Feelings of worthlessness and generalized guilt are symptoms that would prompt consideration for a major depressive episode.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old patient provides a 12-year history of obsessive concerns about dirt, germs, and contamination and spends more than 3 hours a day with washing and cleaning rituals. Which of the following would be preferred as an initial medication treatment?
questions.explanation: The patient's history is consistent with a diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are the preferred initial treatment for this condition.

questions.question_text: A 59-year-old woman is seen for an initial outpatient psychiatric assessment. Her husband says that increasingly over the past 2 years she has seemed less like her usual outgoing self. She has been increasingly apathetic and uninterested in her usual activities, and more recently she has behaved inappropriately in social interactions, making unusual comments and returning home with items that do not belong to her. Recently, her husband has had to begin helping her dress in the morning, and he notes that she is occasionally incontinent of urine. On mental status examination, her affect is blunted and her speech is sparse, although she does not report specific psychotic symptoms or changes in mood. She knows the year and the season but not the month or date, and she has particular difficulty in naming objects. MRI shows prominent frontal and some temporal atrophy with relative sparing of other cortical regions. Which of the following diagnoses is most likely in this patient?
questions.explanation: Of the diagnoses listed, only Pick's disease is among the frontotemporal dementias. It typically begins insidiously, with onset at an earlier age than dementia of the Alzheimer's type. Incontinence and abnormalities of speech and language occur relatively early in the illness course. Symptoms of frontal lobe dysfunction, including apathy and socially inappropriate behaviors, are common. Unlike dementia of the Alzheimer's type, which is associated with more diffuse changes, Pick's disease is characterized by specific frontal and temporal atrophy.

questions.question_text: A Shite decides that a patient with alcohol dependence would benefit from regular laboratory monitoring. Which of the following single tests would best provide information about heavy alcohol use over the preceding 7 to 10 days?
questions.explanation: CDT is more sensitive and specific than the other tests listed. However, better results may be obtained with combined tests (e.g., CDT and gamma-glutamyltransferase—GGT). Because of interpatient variability in the CDT test result, the individual patient is best used as his or her own baseline for CDT.

questions.question_text: A patient with major depression shows no improvement after an adequate trial (in dose and duration) of an antidepressant. The best next step is to:

options.text: conduct a 'washout' by stopping all medication for 4 weeks, and then reassess.
augment the antidepressant with thyroid hormone.
augment with both thyroid hormone and lithium.
switch to a different class of antidepressant.

correct_answer.text: switch to a different class of antidepressant.

correct_answers.text: switch to a different class of antidepressant.

questions.explanation: If a patient shows not even a partial response despite a full therapeutic dose of a particular antidepressant, switching to a different class of antidepressant is advised. Washing out by suddenly stopping all medications will likely precipitate discontinuation symptoms and worsen the patient's status.

questions.question_text: Of the following, which is the most common reason psychiatrists are sued for malpractice?
questions.explanation: Suicide is the most common reason for malpractice litigation against a psychiatrist. Documentation of a proper assessment with consultation helps to provide a reasonable defense.

questions.question_text: Anorexia nervosa is most commonly comorbid with which of the following personality disorders?
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa has been associated with obsessive-compulsive personality disorder and is not typically associated with dependent, paranoid, schizotypal, or histrionic personality disorders.

questions.question_text: The use of which of the following has been associated with hyperparathyroidism?
questions.explanation: Lithium-induced hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism are uncommon but well-established side effects associated with lithium therapy. Both hyperplasia and adenomas of the parathyroid glands have been described in association with lithium therapy.

questions.question_text: Narcolepsy is characterized by which of the following signs and symptoms?

options.text: Sudden episodes of muscle tone loss

correct_answer.text: Sudden episodes of muscle tone loss

correct_answers.text: Sudden episodes of muscle tone loss

questions.explanation: Cataplexy, or sudden loss of muscle tone, is often triggered by strong emotions in patients with narcolepsy. The classic tetrad of narcolepsy includes refreshing sleep attacks, sleep paralysis, and intrusions of REM sleep.

questions.question_text: The four major components of a psychodynamic view of personality disorders are a biologically based temperament, a set of internalized object relations, an enduring sense of self, and:

options.text: a specific constellation of defense mechanisms.

correct_answer.text: a specific constellation of defense mechanisms.

correct_answers.text: a specific constellation of defense mechanisms.

questions.explanation: The psychodynamic clinician views personality disorders as involving four major components: a biologically based temperament, internalized object relations, an enduring sense of self, and a specific constellation of defense mechanisms.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant duloxetine may simultaneously improve mood and:
questions.explanation: Duloxetine is a serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that has demonstrated efficacy in treating both major depression and chronic pain, particularly with conditions like backache and shoulder pain.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old man with a medical history of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is referred for a psychiatric evaluation of his anxiety. For the past month, since the patient's initial evaluation and treatment for GERD, he complains of an increasing sense of unease, nervousness, restlessness, and inability to sit and read the paper. His medications include 20 mg/day of esomeprazole, 10 mg of metoclopramide q.i.d., and 0.5 mg of lorazepam t.i.d. orally or as needed. He is very concerned about his condition because a sibling who had a similar problem died from esophageal carcinoma. Other than being noticeably fidgety, his mental status exam is unremarkable. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Somatoform disorder not otherwise specified (i.e., 'sympathy symptoms' with deceased sibling)

questions.explanation: The description and observation of the inability to be still—that is, motor restlessness—suggests akathisia rather than a simple anxiety or adjustment disorder.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old patient with no prior history of mental health treatment presents with a major depressive episode. Which of the following elements would be the most important in choosing a medication for treatment?

options.text: Co-occurring diagnosis of alcohol dependence in full sustained remission
Suicide attempt by aspirin overdose at age 16
Good antidepressant response to fluoxetine in a first-degree relative

questions.explanation: In deciding on pharmacotherapy of a major depressive episode, it is most important to rule out a diagnosis of bipolar disorder. In such patients, initiation of either lithium or lamotrigine would be a reasonable option.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder has been adequately maintained on lamotrigine. Recently she has experienced an exacerbation of her manic symptoms, and her physician elects to add a second mood stabilizer. Instead of improving, the patient's symptoms worsen. Her serum lamotrigine levels are nearly undetectable. What was the most likely mood stabilizer that was added?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine and oral contraceptives containing ethynyl estradiol induce hepatic enzyme systems that decrease lamotrigine levels. Therefore, if carbamazepine was added, it would likely lead to significantly reduced levels of lamotrigine.

questions.question_text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is hypothesized to involve a neural circuit connecting the cortex and striatum with the:
questions.explanation: Brain imaging studies suggest that obsessive-compulsive disorder involves abnormalities in a cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit. The orbitofrontal cortex plays a major role in the 'worry circuit.'

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychiatric disorders occurs most commonly as a comorbid disorder with anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is associated with depression in 65% of cases, social phobia in 34% of cases, and obsessive-compulsive disorder in 26% of cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the LEAST problematic for the psychiatrist according to ethical principles?

options.text: A psychiatrist in a remote area with no other psychiatrists is involved in a romantic relationship with a patient's adult grandchild.
A psychiatrist convinces a patient who was sexually abused by a former clinician to file a suit against that former clinician and serves as the forensic expert for the patient.
A psychiatrist in a metropolitan area agrees to treat her financial adviser's child.
A psychiatrist hires a current patient to perform clerical work in the psychiatrist's office.

correct_answer.text: A psychiatrist in a remote area with no other psychiatrists is involved in a romantic relationship with a patient's adult grandchild.

correct_answers.text: A psychiatrist in a remote area with no other psychiatrists is involved in a romantic relationship with a patient's adult grandchild.

questions.explanation: While a romantic relationship with a patient's adult grandchild may create a problematic dual role, the psychiatrist does not have the option of referring the patient to another clinician and thus lacks one possible way of avoiding the dual role. Other options present avoidable conflicts of interest or ethical dilemmas.

questions.question_text: In the initial assessment, a psychiatrist is consulted by a lesbian couple seeking help for some problems in their long-standing committed relationship. Which of the following is the best approach for the psychiatrist to take in assessing the possibility of domestic violence within the couple?

options.text: Ask routine questions about battering while taking the history.
Wait until the therapy is well established before asking about it.
Ask about it only when material is presented that suggests the problem.
The topic need not be raised because domestic violence is low in lesbian couples.

correct_answer.text: Ask routine questions about battering while taking the history.

correct_answers.text: Ask routine questions about battering while taking the history.

questions.explanation: Domestic violence in general is underestimated, and it is particularly likely to be overlooked in lesbian couples due to stereotypes. Couples often do not bring it up spontaneously, so routine questions about battering are appropriate.

questions.question_text: A patient is being treated for a cat phobia. The therapist decides to pass by a pet store that has cats several times in a therapeutic context. Which of the following treatment strategies does this behavior illustrate?
questions.explanation: Exposure therapy involves gradual exposure to the feared object or situation, which is effective in reducing anxiety associated with phobias.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive functions is most likely to remain stable with normal aging?
questions.explanation: Language syntax, vocabulary, communication, and store of knowledge tend to remain stable with normal aging, while other cognitive functions may decline.

questions.question_text: A consultation is requested for a 22-year-old man because of a gradual onset of behavioral symptoms that include irritability, aggression, and personality change. Associated findings include mild jaundice, dysarthria, and choreiform movements. The consultant also notices a golden-brown discoloration of the cornea. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Wilson's disease, or hepatolenticular degeneration, is an autosomal recessive disorder of copper metabolism characterized by CNS and hepatic manifestations. Copper deposition in the cornea results in the characteristic Kayser-Fleischer rings.
